beat: progression systems, trackable stats, missable content, RNG, difficulty, multiplayer, version notes

existenceVerification.summary: Real, released title. Announced April 2, 2025 during the Nintendo Switch 2 reveal Direct. Released November 6, 2025, exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2. Developed by Koei Tecmo (Omega Force / AAA Games Studio), published by Nintendo (Koei Tecmo in Japan). Prequel story depicting the 'Imprisoning War' referenced in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, starring Princess Zelda and King Rauru. Metacritic score 79/100 ('Generally Favorable', 105 critic reviews); Famitsu gave it 35/40. Shipped over 1 million copies worldwide as of January 26, 2026.

findings.name: Switch 2 exclusivity
findings.detail: Nintendo's own product page lists the game as a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive with no original Switch version, unlike Breath of the Wild / Tears of the Kingdom / Age of Calamity which all ran on original Switch. File size listed as 43.5 GB. Supports TV, Tabletop, and Handheld modes.

findings.name: Local co-op / split-screen / GameShare
findings.detail: Supports local co-op for 2 players with split-screen on a single system, and Switch 2 GameShare allowing a second player to join via a second console without owning a copy of the game ('only one person needs to have the game'). No mention found of online multiplayer specifically (online functionality, if any, unconfirmed).

findings.name: Multiple difficulty settings + Forbidden Difficulty
findings.detail: Official Nintendo listing states there are 'multiple selectable difficulties', plus a post-game unlockable difficulty tier called 'Forbidden Difficulty'. Exact names/number of standard difficulty tiers below Forbidden not confirmed by any source found.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed whether difficulty selection is shown/tracked anywhere in menus beyond selection itself.

findings.name: No confirmed in-game Medal List
findings.detail: Earlier Hyrule Warriors titles (original Hyrule Warriors, Age of Calamity) featured an in-game 'Medal List' as a pseudo-achievement system. I could not find any source (official page, Wikipedia, reviews) confirming this system exists in Age of Imprisonment, nor confirming it was removed. This is a critical unknown for trophy design.

findings.name: No confirmed overall completion percentage stat
findings.detail: Age of Calamity had a specific quest ('Hope of All Hyrule') showing overall game completion percentage. No equivalent system was found described for Age of Imprisonment in any source checked (official site, Wikipedia, review excerpts).

findings.name: Weapon upgrades via Zonaite Steel
findings.detail: Per Wikipedia's gameplay summary: players use 'spoils' to upgrade characters by assisting the people of ancient Hyrule, and improve weapons with 'Zonaite Steel'. Zonai devices function with a battery mechanic tied to abilities.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed where upgrade progress is displayed (likely a character/weapon menu, unverified).

findings.name: Camps and material submission
findings.detail: Per a Siliconera hands-on review: camps unlock during campaign missions where submitting materials/items provides performance buffs. Weapon/skill upgrades described by the reviewer as 'quite simple' to manage, with no extensive grinding required.

findings.name: Character unlock pacing
findings.detail: Reviewer noted the roster starts limited (around 3 playable characters) and expands to 6+ over the course of the campaign, similar to pacing of prior Hyrule Warriors titles. Exact total roster count not confirmed by any source found.
findings.trackable: Character select screen likely shows unlocked roster (unconfirmed).

findings.name: Confirmed named characters
findings.detail: Characters confirmed by name across sources: Princess Zelda (protagonist), King Rauru, Queen Sonia, Mineru (Zonai-tech focused moveset), Calamo (new character added in Nov 2025 update, teams up with Zelda for a Sync Strike), and three masked Sage characters: Zora Queen Qia, Goron Chief Agraston, Rito Sage Raphica. Ganondorf and a 'Knight Construct' appear in the story per Wikipedia. This is not confirmed to be the full playable roster.

findings.name: Sync Strike
findings.detail: A cooperative attack system: when nearby characters have full Sync gauges, they can perform a joint 'Sync Strike' attack. Inspired by the hand-touch mechanic from Tears of the Kingdom, per director Koki Aoyanagi. The Nov 27, 2025 free update added a new Zelda/Calamo Sync Strike specifically.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed whether Sync Strike usage is counted/tracked anywhere.

findings.name: Large-scale battles
findings.detail: Missions range from brief supply/support tasks to large story campaigns; some battles reportedly feature 500-1,000+ enemies. Players can assign allied characters to different map locations simultaneously to handle multiple objectives at once (per hands-on review).
findings.trackable: Enemy defeat counts likely shown per-mission (standard Warriors-series convention) but not explicitly confirmed for this title.

findings.name: Auto-heal and auto-refill battery toggles
findings.detail: Reviewer mentions optional settings to auto-heal when low on health and auto-refill Zonai device battery. These sound like assist-mode style toggles that could affect trophy eligibility design (similar to how some games disqualify trophies if assist options are on) but no confirmation such a restriction exists here.

findings.name: amiibo support
findings.detail: Official Nintendo store listing confirms amiibo support grants in-game rewards. Specific amiibo/rewards list not found in any source checked.

findings.name: Cross-save bonuses from Age of Calamity and Tears of the Kingdom
findings.detail: Official Nintendo listing states save data from Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom unlocks bonuses in this game. Exact bonuses not detailed in any source found.

findings.name: Free content updates
findings.detail: Nintendo's listing promises free post-launch content updates including additional challenges and Phantom Ganon battles. The first confirmed free update shipped November 27, 2025, adding two new weapons (a spear and a two-handed claymore-style sword), a new Zelda/Calamo Sync Strike, and unspecified 'new challenges' on the map, likely gated behind story progress.

findings.name: Repetitiveness criticism (relevant to completionist trophy pacing)
findings.detail: Metro GameCentral gave a notably low score (40/100), calling the game 'insanely repetitive, horribly shallow, and pointlessly easy' — worth noting for trophy pacing/difficulty assumptions, though this is an outlier opinion versus the 79 Metacritic average.

versionNotes.note: Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment is Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive with no original Switch release, unlike prior mainline Zelda titles (BOTW, TOTK) and the previous Hyrule Warriors spin-off Age of Calamity, all of which ran on original Switch.
GameShare (Switch 2 feature) allows a second local player to join split-screen co-op without owning a copy of the game.

A free content update (Nov 27, 2025) added new weapons and a new Sync Strike combo; Nintendo has committed to further free updates including Phantom Ganon battles, implying additional post-launch content beyond what shipped at launch. Trophy/achievement lists built purely from launch-day information may miss this added content.

gaps: Could not confirm whether the game has any in-game achievement/'Medal List' analog at all (present in earlier Hyrule Warriors titles). This is the single most important unresolved question for downstream trophy design, since per the ruleset a trophy can only be built on something the game displays to the player.
Could not confirm whether an overall completion-percentage stat (like Age of Calamity's 'Hope of All Hyrule') exists.

Could not confirm the total playable character roster count or the full character list — only a partial list of named characters (Zelda, Rauru, Sonia, Mineru, Calamo, Qia, Agraston, Raphica, plus story-only Ganondorf) was found.
Could not confirm the total number of maps, regions, or missions in the campaign.
Could not confirm any missable content — no source discussed permanently-lockable content, time-limited events, or point-of-no-return story choices.
Could not confirm RNG/loot drop systems in any detail (e.g., rare material drop rates, weapon rarity tiers).
Could not confirm whether online multiplayer exists beyond local co-op/GameShare (official source only described local/split-screen/GameShare).
Could not confirm exact names or number of standard difficulty tiers below the post-game 'Forbidden Difficulty'.
